modern: Let it make no difference to you whether you are cold or warm, if you are doing your duty; and whether you are drowsy or have had enough sleep; and whether spoken ill of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else. For it is one of the acts of life, this act by which we die; it is enough, then, in this act too, to do well what we have in hand.
original: Let it make no difference to thee whether thou art cold or warm, if thou art doing thy duty; and whether thou art drowsy or satisfied with sleep; and whether ill-spoken of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else. For it is one of the acts of life, this act by which we die; it is sufficient then in this act also to do well what we have in hand.
